Senses.Explanation: Literally "one" (一) classifier (隻) "eye" (眼): "one eye," attested 992 times in 233 allowlisted texts. The records use it in appraisals with the verbs possess, place, lose, exchange, and open. In the Damei case, Jiashan says, "at Damei I lost one eye" (我當時在大梅，失却一隻眼); Xuedou comments that Jiashan did not know he had then "exchanged for one eye" (換得一隻眼). Another appraisal says Yunmen "possesses only one eye" because he "only looks ahead and does not look behind" (只具一隻眼，只管瞻前，不管照後). Productive forms include "possess one eye" (具一隻眼, 381 occurrences), "place one eye here" (著得一隻眼, 89), "lose one eye" (失却一隻眼, 91), and "open another eye" (別開一隻眼).
Senses.Note: The phrase can expand beyond an individual appraisal. Xuefeng says, "the whole earth is a patch-robed monk's one eye" (盡大地是沙門一隻眼). Other instructions say that placing one eye at a cited point lets one "see seven ways vertically and eight ways horizontally" (便見七縱八橫), or that a staff "opens another eye" for the assembly. The corpus records these predicates and images without supplying a single replacement gloss for eye.
